An open-weight 753B scientific model just reported a win over GPT-6-Astra.

Here are the key technical developments today across open models, developer tooling, and infrastructure.

🧪 Deep Principle released Hydrogen-1.0, a 753B open-weight model for chemistry, materials science, and life sciences. Post-trained on Z.ai's GLM-5.3 using laboratory records and agent trajectories, it ships under an MIT License and reports a FrontierScience-Research win over GPT-6-Astra.

🎮 Anthropic updated Claude Code's system prompt to stop developers from creating video game clones, decompilations, or ports. While retro gaming faces a surge in AI-generated clones, users can still use Claude Code to build original games.

⚡ OpenAI launched the Grid Protectors Program to work with utility providers. The effort aims to help future compute campuses maintain grid reliability and protect consumer electricity costs.

🛡️ OpenAI is increasing Security Bug Bounty rewards for independent researchers. The program now offers higher base payouts alongside bonuses for report quality, loyalty, and targeted priority campaigns.

The rapid rise of domain-specific open weights is reshaping how we think about specialized research tools versus general-purpose frontier models.
